articles.title: Preoperative Sepsis Is Associated With Increased 90-Day and 2-Year Complications Following Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: A Time-Stratified and Organism-Specific Analysis.
articles.authors: Castano AA, Holle AM, Renfree SP, Koschmeder KT, Zeller AM, Hassebrock JD
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national administrative claims database
articles.population: Patients undergoing total shoulder arthroplasty with at least four years of data available
articles.outcomes: 90-day complications (postoperative sepsis, pneumonia, acute kidney injury, deep vein thrombosis, urinary tract infection, readmission, wound dehiscence) and 2-year complications (periprosthetic joint infection, implant loosening, postoperative stiffness)
articles.take_home: Patients who had sepsis in the two years before shoulder surgery had higher rates of complications within 90 days and at two years, with the greatest risk when sepsis occurred within three months of surgery. The type of bacteria causing the sepsis also affected which complications were most likely to occur.

articles.title: Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty for Proximal Humerus Fractures Using the Biomet Comprehensive Shoulder System: One-Year Results Reflect Clinically Meaningful Recovery.
articles.authors: Pasqualini I, Jevnikar BE, Turan O, Tanoira I, Ranalletta M, Rossi LA
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
articles.population: Elderly patients with acute proximal humerus fractures treated with reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Pain (Visual Analog Scale), function (SANE and ASES scores), range of motion (forward flexion and external rotation), and patient acceptable symptom state achievement at one and two years
articles.take_home: Reverse shoulder replacement for upper arm fractures in older patients provided good pain relief and functional improvement by one year, which remained stable at two years. Although most patients recovered well by one year, about a quarter continued to improve further by two years, particularly in pain and shoulder rotation.

articles.title: Whole-Body Compensation Supports Early Functional Hygiene Recovery Despite Persistent Internal Rotation Deficits After Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Morriss NJ, Castle P, Pezzulo JD, Farnam Z, Ramirez G, Mannava S, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary reverse total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Shoulder internal rotation range of motion, task completion time, functional reach distance, trunk and lumbar compensation, muscle activation patterns
articles.take_home: After reverse shoulder replacement, patients regain the ability to perform everyday tasks like reaching behind their back within 6 months, even though their shoulder's internal rotation remains limited. The body compensates by using more trunk and spine movement and changing how muscles work to achieve this functional improvement.

articles.title: Return to riding after open reduction internal fixation of acute clavicle fractures in professional horse jockeys.
articles.authors: Rowse JC, Faulkner H, Hermans D, Duckworth DG
articles.population: Professional horse jockeys with acute clavicle fractures
articles.outcomes: Time to return to riding, DASH score at 12 months, time to radiographic union, time to full range of motion, and complication rates
articles.take_home: Professional jockeys who had surgery to fix broken collarbones returned to riding after about 7 weeks on average, with very good arm function and few complications. The procedure appears safe and effective for this group of athletes.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Arthroscopic Treatment for Shoulder Joint Tuberculosis.
articles.authors: Chen S, Yang Y, Chen J, Zheng F, Jin H, Wang W, et al.
articles.population: Patients with confirmed or clinically suspected shoulder tuberculosis
articles.outcomes: Pain reduction, shoulder function scores (UCLA, ASES, Constant-Murley), recurrence rate, inflammation markers (ESR, CRP)
articles.take_home: Arthroscopic surgery combined with anti-tuberculosis medication significantly reduced pain and improved shoulder function in patients with tuberculosis of the shoulder joint, with only 2 out of 18 patients experiencing recurrence. All patients completed surgery without serious complications and showed good long-term results over an average follow-up of 4.5 years.

articles.title: Clinical and radiographic outcomes of reverse shoulder arthroplasty performed with 40 mm polyethylene glenospheres vs. 36 mm cobalt chrome glenospheres at minimum 2-years follow-up.
articles.authors: Boekel P, Piggott RP, Conyard C, Bale S, Walton M, Monga P, et al.
articles.population: Patients who had reverse shoulder replacement surgery between 2013 and 2022
articles.sample_size: 199 patients (107 with polyethylene glenospheres, 92 with cobalt chrome glenospheres)
articles.outcomes: Oxford Shoulder scores, glenoid radiolucency, notching, revision surgery rates
articles.take_home: At 2 years after surgery, polyethylene glenospheres performed similarly to cobalt chrome glenospheres in terms of shoulder function and pain relief. The cobalt chrome group showed slightly more bone changes around the implant, though neither type of glenosphere was clearly superior overall.

articles.title: Implant selection and fixation in radial head arthroplasty: A qualitative analysis of surgeon decision-making.
articles.authors: Beale H, Abouharb A, Reilly P, Kedgley AE, Sabharwal S
articles.study_type: Qualitative analysis of surgeon decision-making using semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis
articles.population: UK consultant orthopaedic surgeons sub-specialised in upper-limb arthroplasty and elbow surgery
articles.outcomes: Five themes and 13 sub-themes regarding implant selection drivers, fixation philosophy, intraoperative cues, patient profiles and outcomes
articles.take_home: Surgeons use practical, consistent decision-making rules when choosing radial head implants and how to fix them, prioritising bone quality and the ability to adjust for different anatomy. Some important factors that surgeons rely on, such as assessing bone quality during surgery, are not currently measured in research studies.

articles.title: Revision Risk Following Primary Anatomic and Reverse TSA with an Exactech Equinoxe Compared with Other Devices: A U.S.-Based Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Prentice HA, Chang RN, Yian E, Navarro RA, Singh A, Chan DP, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using registry data
articles.population: Adult patients who underwent primary shoulder replacement surgery between 2005 and 2023
articles.sample_size: 13,901 patients (8,707 anatomic replacements, 4,374 reverse replacements for wear, 820 reverse replacements for fracture)
articles.outcomes: Risk of needing revision surgery within the follow-up period
articles.take_home: Patients who received Exactech Equinoxe devices for standard shoulder replacement were nearly twice as likely to need revision surgery compared to other brands, though this risk was not seen with reverse-design replacements. Patients who previously received an Exactech Equinoxe standard replacement should be aware of this finding and discuss it with their surgeon.

articles.title: Knotless and knotted all-suture anchors have comparable clinical outcomes and return to sport rates following arthroscopic anterior labral (Bankart) repair.
articles.authors: Townsend CB, Vega TF, Ithurburn MP, Loeb AE, Atkinson A, Froom R, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing arthroscopic Bankart repair with all-suture anchors
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery rates, return to sport rates, ASES and WOSI scores
articles.take_home: Both knotless and knotted all-suture anchors produced similar results for shoulder labral repair, with no meaningful differences in revision rates, functional scores or ability to return to sport. Among competitive athletes who tried to return to their sport, 95% successfully did so.

articles.title: Osteochondritis dissecans of the glenoid: A case report and review of the literature.
articles.authors: Garra S, Krasovitsky N, Howard MS
articles.population: Adolescent overhead athletes with glenoid osteochondritis dissecans
articles.outcomes: Arthroscopic surgical management with cartilage preservation approach for unstable glenoid lesion that failed conservative treatment
articles.take_home: Osteochondritis dissecans of the shoulder socket is very rare but can occur in young overhead athletes. When conservative treatment fails and the bone lesion is unstable, surgery to preserve the cartilage and restore normal joint surface may be an effective approach.

articles.title: Clinical and radiological outcomes following complete release of the long head of triceps in reverse shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kang HW, Italia K, Sane RM, Price RSM, Ingoe H, Maharaj J, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary reverse shoulder arthroplasty with complete long head of triceps release
articles.outcomes: Triceps strength at 2 years (primary outcome); shoulder range of motion, Constant Score, ASES Score, VAS pain score at 2 years; radiological notching and heterotopic ossification; dislocations and neurovascular injuries
articles.take_home: Complete long head of triceps release during reverse shoulder arthroplasty appears safe, with triceps strength remaining similar to before surgery and patient pain and function improving significantly at 2 years. There were no dislocations or major complications.

articles.title: Immediate Self-Rehabilitation With Versus Without Sling Immobilization After Open Latarjet Procedures for Recurrent Anterior Shoulder Instability: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Goetti P, Bothorel H, Martinho T, Seurot A, Zbinden J, Collin P, et al.
articles.population: Patients with recurrent anterior shoulder instability undergoing open Latarjet surgery
articles.outcomes: Primary: Rowe score. Secondary: pain scores, instability scores, patient satisfaction, range of motion, return to work and sport, graft union, osteolysis
articles.take_home: At 2 years after surgery, patients who did not wear a sling had better shoulder function and satisfaction scores than those who wore a sling for 3 weeks. Both groups recovered well early on, suggesting that avoiding the sling after this type of shoulder surgery may be beneficial.

articles.title: Bone graft augmentation reduces complications in osteosynthesis of proximal humerus fractures: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Daher M, Issa C, Parmar T, Kane L, Satalich JR, Abboud JA
articles.population: Patients undergoing surgery for proximal humerus fractures
articles.sample_size: 350 patients total (175 in graft group, 175 in control group) across 5 randomised controlled trials
articles.outcomes: Complication rates, healing time, and pain levels
articles.take_home: Using bone graft during surgery for proximal humerus fractures significantly reduced complications. When biologic bone grafts were used, patients also healed faster (about 3 weeks quicker) and experienced less pain, but synthetic grafts showed no benefit for healing time or pain.
